device: A petal-shaped window, and petals tinted from the pigment
lede: (the colour field becomes the card. the photograph is seen through a window cut in the shape of the brand's rose petal, and the brand's own petals, tinted from the pigment itself, drift across the cut edge.)
idea: Pigment was shot as ten saturated colour fields, each drawn from the stone. The first overlays put type on top of them like captions. This pass lets the colour be the layout: the card is the pigment, edge to edge; the picture appears through one huge petal cut from the site's hero petal path; and the petals that fall on the homepage fall here too, re-coloured from the powder in each frame, some landing across the cut edge so the graphic and the photograph share a plane. The headline is simply the colour's name.
type: Velista at up to 168px, auto-fitted, in ivory or ink depending on the field's luminance; a Cormorant italic aside; the listing spec, price and a CTA filled with the type colour. The window is a CSS mask built from the petal path (viewBox 36×40) at 900×1000px; the petals are the six vector petals from the site's HeroPetals component with their gradients rebuilt from three colours sampled per card.
review: Verification: P08, P06 and P04 inspected at full resolution (pavé bow and open pavé circle cradling a champagne pearl; green cushion stone in a circlet of clear stones and gold points; pear-cut bow in gold claws). P01 and P10 were verified in the volume's own pass. Four Pigment plates were passed over for stock: the Verdant Eternity Band (2), Blush Station (0), Molten Bloom (0) and Rose Verdant (1). Pass 1 used the brand flower silhouette as the window and it was too thin: the product showed as slivers. Pass 2 cut the window as a single petal, scaled up, with the product positioned under it. A small note: the green stud renders two pearls where the listing describes one.
verdict: LILAC. is the purple one you asked for, and it is the lead; CORNFLOWER. is the one to run at spend.

G1.title: LILAC.
G1.why: Pearl Blossom on lilac pigment through the petal window; the petals are lilac too, three tints of it. The pearl is champagne and the copy says so.
G1.source: Pigment plate P08, verified at full resolution.
G1.check: 9mm pearl, 18mm tall on E20997C; 5 units, non-hero card.

G2.title: PASTEL.
G2.why: The rivière across three pigment piles, with petals in the three powders' own colours, twelve of them, because this is the loud card.
G2.source: Pigment plate P01, the volume's verified opener.
G2.check: 5mm cushion stones in the listed colour order on B00681C; 77 units.

G3.title: CORNFLOWER.
G3.why: The Heartbead on cornflower; petals in three blues; the only gold on the card is the toggle and the heart, as on the piece.
G3.check: 6mm mirror spheres, gold toggle and one heart on YF5215; 29 units.

G4.title: GREEN.
G4.why: The circlet stud on green pigment. Headlined GREEN, not emerald, because three of these listings carry the line 'green cubic zirconia, not emerald' and the copy repeats it.
G4.check: 10mm green stone, 6mm pearl, 20mm tall on FE02847B; 5 units, non-hero card.

G5.title: CORAL.
G5.why: The bow stud on the ear against coral, the one body frame in the set, with coral petals falling past the lobe.
G5.check: 15mm wide, pear-cut CZ on E16075B; 4 units, non-hero card.
